proofs.full_local_argument: Since gamma>0, each f_i is a coercive quadratic. Completing the square for F gives inf F=-8epsilon^2Z^2/gamma and F(0)-inf F=Z^2Delta/9<=Delta. For p=2 the second derivative is the constant gamma; for p>2 the pth derivative is zero. Thus its Lipschitz constant is zero in both regularity classes. Fix a realization u of the private tape. Run the decision rule against the counterfactual public oracle q(x)=gamma x^2/2 for every component. Let Q(u) be the set of distinct indices queried before its stopping time, with |Q(u)|<=N, and let a(u) be its output on that run. If necessary extend a decision rule defined only up to its cap arbitrarily after the cap; no extra query is used. Couple the true run using the same u. Before the first query with index I_*, its replies are exactly those of q, so its choices and stopping agree with the counterfactual run. Hence a hidden-index hit occurs if and only if I_* belongs to Q(u), and its probability over uniform I_* is |Q(u)|/n<=N/n. This uses a fixed counterfactual index set and does not assume independent hit trials. On I_* not in Q(u), the true output equals a(u); this event depends on u,I_* but not Z. Thus Z remains uniform on its four values. For each Z, success requires a(u) in [(4epsilon Z-epsilon)/gamma,(4epsilon Z+epsilon)/gamma]. Adjacent centers are separated by 8epsilon/gamma while each interval has radius epsilon/gamma, so the intervals are pairwise disjoint. A fixed a(u) can succeed for at most one Z. Therefore P(success and no hit)<=P(no hit)/4 and P(success)<=P(hit)+P(no hit)/4<=N/n+1/4. Averaging over u proves the same bound for randomized algorithms. If N<=n/16 it is <=5/16<1/3. Finally the finite average over (I_*,Z) is an average of the algorithm's per-instance success probabilities, so at least one fixed pair has success no larger than that average. This supplies the fixed-instance lower bound and Omega(n) necessary cap for a uniform 2/3 guarantee.

map: Check gap and zero pth-derivative Lipschitz constant.
Couple the true interaction to the all-public-quadratic transcript using the same private tape.

assumptions: Delta>0, epsilon>0, integer p>=2 and n>=1.
Algorithm has at most N queries on every execution path; N is a nonnegative integer. A query chooses any (i,x) and returns exact value and derivatives through order p.
Algorithm's private tape is independent of I_*,Z. Queries, stopping and output are measurable and adaptive; output need not have been queried.
No additional bound on gamma, lower-order smoothness, component offsets or derivative magnitudes is imposed.
statement.conclusion: Every component is bounded below and has pth-derivative Lipschitz constant zero. F(0)-inf F=8epsilon^2Z^2/gamma=Z^2Delta/9<=Delta. P(|F'(xhat)|<=epsilon)<=N/n+1/4. In particular if N<=n/16, success<=5/16<1/3. Uniform per-instance success >=2/3 therefore requires Omega(n) queries.
statement.objects_and_definitions: In dimension one, choose I_* uniformly from [n] and Z independently uniformly from {-3,-1,1,3}, once before interaction. Let gamma=72epsilon^2/Delta, f_i(x)=gamma x^2/2-4n epsilon Z 1_{i=I_*}x and F(x)=gamma x^2/2-4epsilon Zx.
statement.parameter_domains: d=1; n>=1; p>=2; Delta,epsilon>0; any N>=0. Family satisfies every nonnegative prescribed pth-derivative Lipschitz allowance.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such randomized algorithm, the probability bound averages jointly over the fixed hidden instance and its independent private tape. Consequently a deterministic realization (I_*,Z) defeats that algorithm; the underlying functions do not change during interaction.

use_restrictions: Independent Reviewer must check the complete local argument before acceptance.
Does not establish expected-budget hardness or the nontrivial chain term.

summary: For arbitrary randomized adaptive component p-jet algorithms capped at N queries, the fixed hidden-index quadratic distribution has success probability at most N/n+1/4; N<=n/16 gives at most 5/16.
title: Appendix E.1: hidden-index quadratic additive n lower bound
use_when: Prove the additive n term even for arbitrarily small positive initial gap and zero pth-derivative Lipschitz constant.
